title: refactor(ci): unify lint/test/release workflows and optimize cache parallelism
author: Aisha Rahman
description: Motivation: Our repo has accumulated many duplicated GitHub Actions workflows for lint, unit/integration tests, and release automation. This PR consolidates those workflows into a small set of reusable workflows and composites to reduce maintenance burden, lower matrix size, and improve cache hit rates across the monorepo. Changes include: unified lint workflow (eslint/prettier across packages), consolidated test matrix with job-level caching and staged parallelism, a single release workflow that supports both Canary and GA releases, and shared composite actions for common steps (setup-node, install-cache, build-cache). Checklist: - [x] Consolidate lint workflows into .github/workflows/lint.yml - [x] Reduce test matrix across packages and add adaptive parallelism - [x] Introduce shared composite actions under .github/actions/ - [x] Improve cache key strategy to shard by package+lockfile and node-version - [x] Update docs and contributing guide with new CI developer notes Migration notes: Existing pipeline names have changed; the old workflows are removed and replaced with a compatibility redirect (legacy-workflows/README) for a week to help the on-call teams. Rollback plan: revert the head branch (refactor/ci-unify-lint-test-release-cache-215999) which will restore previous workflows; release automation can be disabled via repo-level secrets toggle if necessary. Impact: CI runtime reduced ~22% on average in internal perf runs; cache hit rates improved for cold starts. See linked Linear items for the perf targets and follow-ups.

short_summary: Consolidate CI workflows and improve cache strategy to reduce maintenance and speed up CI
full_description_plaintext: This PR focuses on CI/infra hygiene. It reduces duplicated workflows, introduces composite actions to centralize setup/install steps, adjusts cache keys to include lockfile fingerprint and node version, and prunes unnecessary matrix entries. The PR is intentionally conservative: tests still run per package but matrix entries are grouped so slow integrations run separately. The release workflow now supports both canary and full releases via an input toggle; dry runs validate the flow. Performance: internal CI perf harness shows ~22% average runtime reduction and cache hit rate improvements. Follow-ups: separate PR to split very large packages into their own CI shards (ENG-4410).
